+# Interactive full-loop vs pulse workers: solve throughput (2026-11-18)
+
+Question: interactive sessions asked to "solve this full-loop" seem to close
+issues faster than pulse workers. Should pulse/workers be simplified?
+
+Evidence is GitHub search counts (`is:issue is:closed reason:completed`, split by
+`solved:worker` / `solved:interactive`) plus the timelines of the slow
+interactive solves. "Product repo" is a large private managed repository. Its
+name is withheld.
+
+## Weekly solves (closed as completed)
+
+| Week ending | framework worker | framework interactive | framework issues created interactively | product worker | product interactive | product issues created by workers |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 10-28 | 147 | 54 | 126 | 505 | 56 | 1002 |
+| 11-04 | 219 | 124 | 264 | 356 | 95 | 615 |
+| 11-11 | 345 | 134 | 346 | 520 | 174 | 560 |
+| 11-18 | 331 | 215 | 470 | 1496 | 91 | 2188 |

+  product repo's worker output nearly tripled in the last week.
+- Interactive solves are rising in the framework repo because interactive
+  sessions now create most of its issues (470 last week) and solve their own
+  filings in the same session (median close 1.1h). They solve work they have
+  just discovered, while its context is loaded. They are not competing with
+  workers for the existing backlog.
+- Worker dispatch latency is not the bottleneck: on 2026-11-18 a new framework
+  issue was worker-dispatched about 90s after filing.

This code came from the already merged #38999 (GH#38997). It appears here only because the incremental review range included the rebase onto `main`; this PR does not touch worker-lifecycle files.

This trade-off was raised and decided during #38999's review. In the root-sshd branch of `require_predating_daemon`, `AIDEVOPS_PROTECTED_PROC_INSPECTION=1` requires descriptor evidence, so an inherited worktree log descriptor refuses removal. Without the opt-in the exemption applies, so unrelated newer logins do not block retirement in default configurations. The accepted residual risk is limited to that opt-out default. This is a recorded policy decision, not an oversight, so it is not reopened here. GH#39013 (t19107) explicitly keeps that behaviour while fixing the related age-first ordering for older root sessions under the opt-in.

@@ -1554,15 +1554,94 @@ _tbr_pending_discovery_stages() {

+# GH#39010: classify the queue once per run (tier 1 = standing human_decision).
+# When any entry is decided, tier 0 ends early enough to leave tier 1 about a
+# quarter of the remaining queue window; tier 1 also gets whatever tier 0 does
+# not use. Without this, a tier 0 that never finishes inside the window meant
+# tier 1 was never scanned, so replies, policy changes and trusted retries on
+# decided holds could never wake them. Two batched jq reads (queue identities,
+# then decision wakes) keep the prepass at a constant process count: on a
+# 129-entry queue they take ~40ms where per-entry reads took ~1.5s, which the
+# old per-tier scan repeated on every traversal. An unreadable file falls back
+# to the per-entry check, never to a guessed tier. Below four seconds a quarter
+# rounds to nothing, so tier 0 keeps the whole window. Runs inside the scope of
+# _tbr_pending_scan_queue (decided_set, tier0_deadline).
+_tbr_pending_classify() {
+	local file="" share=0 ids="" wakes="" decided_paths=";" i=0
+	local name repo issue
+	local -a files=() names=() decisions=()
+	decided_set=";"
+	tier0_deadline="$TBR_QUEUE_DEADLINE"
+	for file in "${TBR_ROOT}"/queue/*.json; do
+		[[ ! -f "$file" ]] || files+=("$file")
+	done
+	[[ "${#files[@]}" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
+	if ids=$(jq -r '[(input_filename | split("/") | last), (.repo // "" | tostring),
+		(.issue // "" | tostring)] | @tsv' "${files[@]}" 2>/dev/null); then
+		while IFS=$'\t' read -r name repo issue; do
+			[[ -n "$name" && -n "$repo" && -n "$issue" ]] || continue
+			# Same key as _tbr_key, without a subshell per entry.
+			file="${TBR_ROOT}/decisions/${repo//\//--}--${issue}.json"
+			[[ -f "$file" ]] || continue
+			names+=("$name")
+			decisions+=("$file")
+		done <<<"$ids"
+	else
+		for file in "${files[@]}"; do
+			! _tbr_entry_decided "$file" || decided_set+="${file##*/};"
+		done
+	fi
+	if [[ "${#decisions[@]}" -gt 0 ]]; then
+		if wakes=$(jq -r 'select(.wake == "human_decision") | input_filename' "${decisions[@]}" 2>/dev/null); then
+			while IFS= read -r file; do
+				[[ -z "$file" ]] || decided_paths+="${file};"
+			done <<<"$wakes"
+			for i in "${!names[@]}"; do
+				case "$decided_paths" in *";${decisions[$i]};"*) decided_set+="${names[$i]};" ;; esac
+			done
+		else
+			for name in "${names[@]}"; do
+				! _tbr_entry_decided "${TBR_ROOT}/queue/${name}" || decided_set+="${name};"
+			done
+		fi
+	fi
+	[[ "$decided_set" != ";" ]] || return 0
+	share=$(((TBR_QUEUE_DEADLINE - SECONDS) / 4))
+	[[ "$share" -ge 1 ]] || return 0
body:
Fixed in 40478b7400. When decided entries exist, `_tbr_pending_reserve` reserves `max(1, remaining / 4)` seconds once at least two seconds remain, so tier 1 now gets a turn on 2-7 second windows. With a single second left, the second goes to tier 0. A 1-second reservation would give each tier nothing usable, and tier 1 still gets any time tier 0 leaves.

Verified with a 3-second budget, 12 undecided entries and 1 decided entry: tier 0 runs first, the decided entry is checked, and `rearm_cursor_decided` is written. A 1-second window gives no reservation. Results were stable across 3 runs.

body:
Fixed in 40478b7400. When the reservation itself cuts a tier-0 entry short (rc >= 2, the tier-0 deadline is earlier than the queue deadline, and that deadline has been reached), `_tbr_pending_park` does three things:

- parks the tier-0 cursor just before the entry, so the next run starts with it;
- writes a `<cursor>_full_window` marker naming the entry;
- stops tier 0, so tier 1 keeps its reservation in that run.

The coordinator does not resume tier 0 after parking, because resuming would move the cursor past the entry.

On the next run, `_tbr_pending_reserve` sees the marker and gives tier 0 the whole queue window. A pending pass clears the marker. A `--count` probe only reads it, so the trigger probe also gets the full window, and the marker stays for the pass that acts on the entry. A held `--count` cursor (GH#39006) is left in place, because it already sits before an earlier counted entry.

Worst case: an entry that needs more than the whole window alternates between a reserved run and a full-window run. Neither tier then waits more than every other run, where before tier 0 repeated the same timeout on every pulse.

Verified over three consecutive runs. The entry needs 9 seconds, the window is 10 seconds and the tier-0 share is about 8 seconds.

1. Run 1: the entry is cut short, the marker names it, the cursor is parked at the start of the queue, and tier 1 is still reached.
2. Run 2: the entry is checked first and completes, and the marker is cleared.
3. Run 3: the rotation moves on.

All of this was stable across 3 repeats. The existing suites still pass: `test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` 62/0, `test-recovery-policy.sh` 35/0, and the GH#39006 cursor checks 7/7.

** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Heavy lift** **Predating root `sshd-session` exemption does not rule out a live worktree descriptor.** Under `AIDEVOPS_PROTECTED_PROC_INSPECTION=1`, a root `sshd-session` that predates `.git` skips `require_protected_references`. Process age bounds only when the process started. It does not bound later file opens. When `cwd` is unreadable, the census takes the denied-reference path. It reaches `require_predating_daemon` before any `fd` scan, so a worktree descriptor opened after startup is not checked. Worktree retirement can then proceed while that session holds the descriptor. Choose one of these behaviors and document it in the code: - Establish that these sessions cannot acquire or keep worktree references after startup, and cite that restriction in the code path. - Keep a live-reference check for the denied `cwd` case, or record that the issue accepts this risk.
Scope

This finding is narrow. It requires opt-in, a root `sshd-session` that predates `.git`, an unreadable `cwd`, and a worktree descriptor opened after startup. The skip itself matches issue `#39013`, so this comment asks for an explicit safety decision and does not request a code change.

That includes creating or removing a direct entry in `.git`, such as a lock file. A root-forked `sshd-session` that started after `.git` was created can therefore pass this check after any later change to `.git`. The skip on line 115 then bypasses `require_protected_references` under opt-in, even when the session holds a worktree log descriptor. Cleanup can then proceed while that reference is live. -   their queue entries; corrected briefs preserve the original audit record.

-

-

-once, when the task revision differs from the observed one or a trusted retry
-follows the observation. That happens within the pass interval below, and the
-brief owner changes no label. For any other sanctioned manual transition use
-`gh-write-helper.sh issue status <N> --repo <owner/repo> available`, never a
-raw label edit.
-

-runner that opened it queues the issue (`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`;
-circuits it authored are backfilled every 6h) and its pulse supervisor runs

-`PULSE_LLM_RECOVERY_INTERVAL`, default 3h). `pending` re-verifies each entry on

-reads for issues whose `updated_at` has not advanced since its last complete
-held check. API secondary cooldown or an active GraphQL circuit breaker defers
-the pass until pressure clears; a partial queue resumes on the next interval.

-1. Read the public observation and the entry's `local_excerpts` (protected
-   evidence; excerpts are matched by issue number, so confirm the repository).
-   Classify the real cause; the reported class is often a symptom.
-2. **Brief defect** (missing/wrong Files Scope, stale verification, impossible
-   acceptance): make the minimal issue-body revision under brief-author
-   authority. A relevant revision re-arms the circuit; no retry directive needed.
-   A requirement to salvage checkpoint commits or branches that no remote ref
-   holds is impossible acceptance for every other runner: rewrite it as
-   best-effort recovery with the functional spec as source of truth
-   (GH#35871).

-   push transport, a guard blocking its own fix): fix it when in scope, or
-   deduplicate/file a worker-ready framework issue and link it with
-   `blocked-by`. Post `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` only after the fix is live.

-   (defaults, naming, reversible choices, scope interpretation) and revise the
-   brief, which re-arms the circuit. Otherwise name the exact missing input and
-   its owner (user, contributor, maintainer or admin) on the issue once.
-   Closing an investigation as not reproduced is delegated: when its only
-   missing input is a recurrence and none was observed for 72h after its
-   diagnostics merged, close it with that evidence and the recurrence signal
-   that should reopen it (GH#35871).

-   Name the smallest human input on the issue (for example an interactive
-   `aidevops setup --scope source-access`) and record `wake: human_decision`.

-   OWNER/MEMBER comment or a brief revision wakes it (GH#36342).

-   record <repo> <issue>` with stdin `{"wake","next_action","evidence"}`
-   (`wake`: `brief_revision`, `environment_fix`, `owner_change`,
-   `dependency_change` or `human_decision`). A decision suppresses
-   re-assessment for 24h; unchanged blockers are not retried blindly. A plain
-   OWNER/MEMBER reply newer than a `human_decision` (no signature footer or
-   automation marker) ends that suppression on the next supervisor pass, so
-   a maintainer answers on the issue, not in a session (GH#38311).
-
-Unclassified holds (GH#37978): a blocked label is not an instruction. Entries
-with `intake: unclassified_hold` are open issues whose only dispatch stop is
-`status:blocked`, unchanged for a day (`BLOCKER_RECOVERY_UNCLASSIFIED_MIN_AGE`),

-them; missing evidence is never its reason to release. Read the body, the
-`status:blocked` label timeline and trusted OWNER/MEMBER comments, then take
-exactly one outcome and record it with `record`:
-
-- **A reason exists and still holds**: record the decision. If no public
-  comment states it, post one naming the reason, who or what must act, and the
-  wake condition.
-- **The reason no longer holds, or none exists and nothing blocks the work**:
-  re-read the labels and continue only when `status:blocked` is present and
-  `status:in-progress` is absent. Then run
-  `gh-write-helper.sh issue status <N> --repo <owner/repo> available` and
-  post one receipt naming the evidence read. Never release when a trusted
-  OWNER/MEMBER comment made after the label states a hold that still applies.

-  with `wake: human_decision`.

-`needs-maintainer-permissions`, `no-auto-dispatch` or `parent-task`; issues

-excerpts or secret names. A wrong release costs one worker run, whose blocker

-`status:blocked`, gains another hold label or gains a terminal-blocker record.

-  take one outcome:

-    `hold-for-review`, and set `status:available` when nothing else blocks.
-  - **Retire**: close as not planned, citing the reply.
-  - **Keep holding**: record it; post nothing new.
-  - **Question or ambiguous**: answer from evidence or post the canonical ask below once.
-  - **Not a decision** (a script's notice posted with the maintainer's

-

-  queued again. Record the decision with `record` (resume: `brief_revision`;
-  keep or ask: `human_decision`).

-  day ago (`BLOCKER_RECOVERY_HOLD_EXPLAIN_AGE`) and no trusted comment from an

-  the issue that holds the decision ("The decision and evidence are on #N").
-  Never remove the hold for this intake. Record `wake: human_decision`.
-

Option bullets and `**Recommended path:** <option>` may follow. `/decisions` reads exactly this canonical ask line. It discovers issues only by `needs-maintainer-input`, `needs-maintainer-permissions` or `needs-credentials`; when the issue carries only `status:blocked` or `hold-for-review`, add `needs-maintainer-input` (owner: maintainer) with the ask so it reaches the queue.

-Never act on another login's comment, an untrusted comment, or a reply
-older than the label. A reply never grants permissions, credentials, spend or
-publication beyond what the maintainer could approve on that issue. The
-entries retire when the hold or its intake no longer matches, or once a
-decision is recorded after queueing. Public comments carry no local paths.
-
-Repo-delegated queue policy (GH#35129): before terminal-blocker or
-integration-recovery assessment, run `recovery-policy-helper.sh <repo>`. Exit 0

-partial PR, and specifically pre-authorized brief repairs. Record holds with

-OWNER/MEMBER circuits opened by another runner, and entries with
-`intake: remote_observation` are holds only another runner observed (GH#36114);
-`intake: unclassified_hold` entries (above) have no observation at all. Use only
-public issue/PR evidence for all three.

-
-A `[NET-TIER]` loopback denial is a routing hint, not a terminal blocker. Never
-release with `status:blocked`, `permission_required` or a draft checkpoint
-because of it alone. Follow the route the denial names: keep the server running
-in an `aidevops_bounded_operation` and retry the probe once the port listens,
-run server and client inside one bounded operation, or use the registered
-local-hosting site. Report a blocker only after those routes have been tried and
-failed, or when the denial says a whole-process egress backend is active, with
-the denial text and the attempted route as evidence. Details:
-`services/hosting/local-hosting.md` "Headless worker verification access".
+Full rules (initial-map vs binding restrictions, recovery procedure, `#### Coordinator intake`, `#### Terminal-blocker recovery`, `#### Recoverable policy denials (GH#33969)`) live in `reference/worker-integration-recovery.md` "Integration scope recovery". Load it before any undeclared edit, adjacent-integration recovery, `INTEGRATION_RECOVERY_REQUEST`, terminal-blocker handling or coordinator intake. Key invariant: Files Scope is an initial map unless trusted instructions explicitly restrict it; explicit hard boundaries, permissions, credentials, spending, destructive/external actions and security guarantees are never widened.

-   authority. A relevant revision re-arms the circuit; no retry directive needed.
-   A requirement to salvage checkpoint commits or branches that no remote ref
-   holds is impossible acceptance for every other runner: rewrite it as
-   best-effort recovery with the functional spec as source of truth
-   (GH#35871).
-3. **Environment defect** (pinned runtime, dependencies, validator timeouts,
-   push transport, a guard blocking its own fix): fix it when in scope, or
-   deduplicate/file a worker-ready framework issue and link it with
-   `blocked-by`. Post `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` only after the fix is live.
-4. **Input required**: first decide whatever delegated AI authority covers
-   (defaults, naming, reversible choices, scope interpretation) and revise the
-   brief, which re-arms the circuit. Otherwise name the exact missing input and
-   its owner (user, contributor, maintainer or admin) on the issue once.
-   Closing an investigation as not reproduced is delegated: when its only
-   missing input is a recurrence and none was observed for 72h after its
-   diagnostics merged, close it with that evidence and the recurrence signal
-   that should reopen it (GH#35871).
-5. **Permission, secret, spend or trust boundary**: never grant or work around.
-   Name the smallest human input on the issue (for example an interactive
-   `aidevops setup --scope source-access`) and record `wake: human_decision`.
-   A spend, billing or credential-route decision only a maintainer can make is
-   `input_required` with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_INPUT_OWNER=maintainer` (or `admin`):
-   it re-arms on a brief or dependency revision, never on a time window.
-   `permission_required` stays for runtime tool-permission denials. Without a
-   published permission request it re-arms once per backoff window, but only
-   until that re-arm repeats the same result; then a trusted retry, a new
-   OWNER/MEMBER comment or a brief revision wakes it (GH#36342).
-6. Record exactly one decision per entry: `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh
-   record <repo> <issue>` with stdin `{"wake","next_action","evidence"}`
-   (`wake`: `brief_revision`, `environment_fix`, `owner_change`,
-   `dependency_change` or `human_decision`). A decision suppresses
-   re-assessment for 24h; unchanged blockers are not retried blindly. A plain
-   OWNER/MEMBER reply newer than a `human_decision` (no signature footer or
-   automation marker) ends that suppression on the next supervisor pass, so
-   a maintainer answers on the issue, not in a session (GH#38311).
-
-Unclassified holds (GH#37978): a blocked label is not an instruction. Entries
-with `intake: unclassified_hold` are open issues whose only dispatch stop is
-`status:blocked`, unchanged for a day (`BLOCKER_RECOVERY_UNCLASSIFIED_MIN_AGE`),
-with no open dependency and no terminal-blocker record. The helper only queues
-them; missing evidence is never its reason to release. Read the body, the
-`status:blocked` label timeline and trusted OWNER/MEMBER comments, then take
-exactly one outcome and record it with `record`:
-
-- **A reason exists and still holds**: record the decision. If no public
-  comment states it, post one naming the reason, who or what must act, and the
-  wake condition.
-- **The reason no longer holds, or none exists and nothing blocks the work**:
-  re-read the labels and continue only when `status:blocked` is present and
-  `status:in-progress` is absent. Then run
-  `gh-write-helper.sh issue status <N> --repo <owner/repo> available` and
-  post one receipt naming the evidence read. Never release when a trusted
-  OWNER/MEMBER comment made after the label states a hold that still applies.
-- **Only a person can resolve it**: post the canonical public ask below once,
-  with `wake: human_decision`.
-
-Unclassified-hold handling never removes `hold-for-review`, `needs-maintainer-review`,
-`needs-maintainer-permissions`, `no-auto-dispatch` or `parent-task`; issues
-carrying them are never queued as `unclassified_hold`. Public comments carry no local paths,
-excerpts or secret names. A wrong release costs one worker run, whose blocker
-exit then records the reason. The entry retires once the issue closes, loses
-`status:blocked`, gains another hold label or gains a terminal-blocker record.
-
-Maintainer replies on held issues (GH#38311): a `hold-for-review` issue waits
-for a maintainer decision, and a reply on the issue is that decision. The
-helper queues two intakes on the supervisor pass only, never `rearm`, and
-skips issues that also carry `needs-maintainer-review`,
-`needs-maintainer-permissions`, `status:in-progress` or `status:claimed`:
-
-- **`answered_hold`**: this runner's own OWNER/MEMBER login posted a comment
-  after the latest hold label with no signature footer and no automation
-  marker; `reply_comment_id` names it. That login is the maintainer this runner
-  serves, so carry out exactly what the reply decides and nothing broader.
-  Read the hold reason (body and trusted comments before the label), then
-  take one outcome:
-  - **Revise or resume**: persist the revision in the brief, remove
-    `hold-for-review`, and set `status:available` when nothing else blocks.
-  - **Retire**: close as not planned, citing the reply.
-  - **Keep holding**: record it; post nothing new.
-  - **Question or ambiguous**: answer from evidence or post the canonical ask below once.
-  - **Not a decision** (a script's notice posted with the maintainer's
-    token): record it and post nothing.
-
-  Every public outcome posts one receipt containing
-  `<!-- aidevops:hold-reply:<reply_comment_id> -->`, so the reply is never
-  queued again. Record the decision with `record` (resume: `brief_revision`;
-  keep or ask: `human_decision`).
-- **`unexplained_hold`**: this runner's login applied the hold more than a
-  day ago (`BLOCKER_RECOVERY_HOLD_EXPLAIN_AGE`) and no trusted comment from an
-  hour before the label onward states why. Post one decision packet: reason,
-  owner, smallest input, **Recommended path:** and wake condition, or point to
-  the issue that holds the decision ("The decision and evidence are on #N").
-  Never remove the hold for this intake. Record `wake: human_decision`.
-
-For each public ask above, use `**Still needed (owner: maintainer|admin|user|contributor)**: <one-line ask>`, choosing one owner. Option bullets and `**Recommended path:** <option>` may follow. `/decisions` reads exactly this canonical ask line. It discovers issues only by `needs-maintainer-input`, `needs-maintainer-permissions` or `needs-credentials`; when the issue carries only `status:blocked` or `hold-for-review`, add `needs-maintainer-input` (owner: maintainer) with the ask so it reaches the queue.
-
-Never act on another login's comment, an untrusted comment, or a reply
-older than the label. A reply never grants permissions, credentials, spend or
-publication beyond what the maintainer could approve on that issue. The
-entries retire when the hold or its intake no longer matches, or once a
-decision is recorded after queueing. Public comments carry no local paths.
-
-Repo-delegated queue policy (GH#35129): before terminal-blocker or
-integration-recovery assessment, run `recovery-policy-helper.sh <repo>`. Exit 0
-returns the actions the repo enabled in its pinned default-branch policy
-section; only those are delegated authority. Exit 3 (none declared) or 1
-(invalid/unavailable) leaves the steps above unchanged. Apply
-[Repo recovery policy](recovery-policy.md) for exhausted-outlier chain holds
-with independent dependant repoints, session-budget splits after a merged
-partial PR, and specifically pre-authorized brief repairs. Record holds with
-`wake=human_decision`, splits/repoints with `wake=dependency_change`, brief
-repairs with `wake=brief_revision`. Entries with `intake: policy_remote` are
-OWNER/MEMBER circuits opened by another runner, and entries with
-`intake: remote_observation` are holds only another runner observed (GH#36114);
-`intake: unclassified_hold` entries (above) have no observation at all. Use only
-public issue/PR evidence for all three.
-
-#### Recoverable policy denials (GH#33969)
-
-A `[NET-TIER]` loopback denial is a routing hint, not a terminal blocker. Never
-release with `status:blocked`, `permission_required` or a draft checkpoint
-because of it alone. Follow the route the denial names: keep the server running
-in an `aidevops_bounded_operation` and retry the probe once the port listens,
-run server and client inside one bounded operation, or use the registered
-local-hosting site. Report a blocker only after those routes have been tried and
-failed, or when the denial says a whole-process egress backend is active, with
-the denial text and the attempted route as evidence. Details:
-`services/hosting/local-hosting.md` "Headless worker verification access".
+Full rules (initial-map vs binding restrictions, recovery procedure, `#### Coordinator intake`, `#### Terminal-blocker recovery`, `#### Recoverable policy denials (GH#33969)`) live in `reference/worker-integration-recovery.md` "Integration scope recovery". Load it before any undeclared edit, adjacent-integration recovery, `INTEGRATION_RECOVERY_REQUEST`, terminal-blocker handling or coordinator intake. Key invariant: Files Scope is an initial map unless trusted instructions explicitly restrict it; explicit hard boundaries, permissions, credentials, spending, destructive/external actions and security guarantees are never widened.

The following `if` treats every value other than `allow` as an outside-workspace session. The child then unwinds into the parent's `main()` flow, keeps running the fixture logic, and may print a duplicate report. The parent's `ready.read()` also blocks without a timeout, because the parent still holds the write end of the pipe. Close the unused pipe ends and wrap each child body in `try/finally: os._exit(1)`. +		line=$(grep -E -m 1 '^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z]*Error( \[[A-Z_]+\])?:' "$log_file" 2>/dev/null) || line=""

+	[[ "$budget" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
+	dir=$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null) || return 1
+	if ! printf '%s\n' "$budget" >"${dir}/budget"; then
+		rm -rf "$dir"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	printf '%s\n' "$dir"
+	return 0
+}
+
+# Args: issue number, repo slug
+# Returns: 0 when the candidate holds a slot (or no gate is active), 1 when all
+# slots are held. Lost or unreadable loop state fails closed (defer, no claim).
+_dispatch_launch_slot_acquire() {
+	local issue="$1" repo="$2" dir="${_DISPATCH_LAUNCH_SLOT_DIR:-}" budget="" key="" n=0
+	[[ -n "$dir" ]] || return 0
+	key=$(_dispatch_launch_slot_key "$issue" "$repo")
+	[[ ! -f "${dir}/held.${key}" ]] || return 0
+	read -r budget <"${dir}/budget" 2>/dev/null || budget=""
+	if [[ "$budget" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+		for ((n = 1; n <= budget; n++)); do
+			mkdir "${dir}/slot.${n}" 2>/dev/null || continue
+			# An overflow launch (settle) shrinks the budget; back off rather
+			# than launch past it. Concurrent acquirers may both back off.
+			if (($(_dispatch_launch_slots_taken) > budget)); then
+				rmdir "${dir}/slot.${n}" 2>/dev/null || true
+				break
+			fi
+			printf '%s\n' "$n" >"${dir}/held.${key}"
+			return 0
+		done
+	fi
+	: >"${dir}/deferred.${key}" 2>/dev/null || true
+	return 1
+}
+
+# Keep the slot for a launch (rc 0) or an unknown launch state (rc 124, the
+# per-candidate timeout kill); release it otherwise. A success that never
+# acquired (a launch path outside _dlw_claim_slot_and_lock) still takes an
+# overflow slot, so the loop stops instead of launching past the budget.
+# Args: issue number, repo slug, candidate return code
+_dispatch_launch_slot_settle() {
+	local issue="$1" repo="$2" rc="$3" dir="${_DISPATCH_LAUNCH_SLOT_DIR:-}" key="" n=""
+	[[ -n "$dir" && -d "$dir" ]] || return 0
+	key=$(_dispatch_launch_slot_key "$issue" "$repo")
+	if [[ -f "${dir}/held.${key}" ]]; then
+		[[ "$rc" == "0" || "$rc" == "124" ]] && return 0
+		read -r n <"${dir}/held.${key}" 2>/dev/null || n=""
+		if [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+			rmdir "${dir}/slot.${n}" 2>/dev/null || true
+		fi
+		rm -f "${dir}/held.${key}"
+		return 0

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Stop the sudo-session fixture when container setup fails.** The container script does not stop when a setup command fails. If the requested `--uid` is already assigned in the image, `useradd` fails and `alice` is not created. The following `chown` and `su` commands also fail, but the script continues. The final case then exits 0, and the host reports a successful run with `(no kick observed)`. The default UID 1000 does not collide, but any UID that the image already uses does. Enable fail-fast behavior in the container script so that a failed setup step ends the run with a non-zero status. The host already reports any non-zero container exit as exit 2.
